facts.statement: The genus Duerosuchus was named after the Duero River because its fossils were found in the Duero River Basin.
facts.quote: The genus was first described by Andrés and Santiago in 2009 and was named after the Duero River, as it was found in the Duero River Basin.

facts.statement: The type species D. piscator was named based on the inference that the animal could catch fish, deduced from the shape of its teeth.
facts.quote: The type species is D. piscator, named in reference to its presumed ability to catch fish, inferred from the shape of its teeth.

facts.statement: Fossils of Duerosuchus were found in Corrales del Vino, Spain, and date to the Middle Eocene, approximately 40 million years ago.
facts.quote: Remains have been found from Corrales del Vino in Zamora, Spain, and are middle Eocene in age (about 40 million years ago).

facts.statement: The skull of Duerosuchus measures approximately 20 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The skull of Duerosuchus is around 20 cm long.

facts.statement: The total estimated length of Duerosuchus is around 1.6 meters.
facts.quote: The length of the entire animal is estimated to have been around 1.6 m.

facts.statement: Duerosuchus possessed sharp, recurved teeth with narrow bases.
facts.quote: The teeth are sharp and recurved with narrow bases.

facts.statement: The osteoderms of Duerosuchus are typically rectangular with a medial crest running longitudinally along most of the dorsal surface, though an oval shape also occurs.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos o escudos óseos del género tienden a la forma rectangular (apareciendo un segundo morfotipo de contorno ovalado), y suelen presentar una cresta medial que recorre longitudinalmente gran parte de la superficie dorsal.

facts.statement: Although Duerosuchus may have eaten turtles, it was better adapted to prey on smaller animals like fish.
facts.quote: While Duerosuchus may also have preyed on turtles, it was better adapted to catching smaller prey such as fish.

facts.statement: The lack of Duerosuchus fossils in other Eocene deposits on the Iberian Peninsula makes it difficult to determine its chronological and stratigraphic distribution.
facts.quote: La ausencia de indicios del género en otros depósitos del Eoceno de la península ibérica dificulta las conclusiones sobre su distribución cronoestratigráfica.

facts.statement: Duerosuchus was placed in the family Planocraniidae following a 2021 phylogenetic study, resolving earlier uncertainty about its classification.
facts.quote: However, the genus was not initially included in a phylogenetic study and its position within Crocodilia was uncertain, until a 2021 study recovered Duerosuchus within the family Planocraniidae.

facts.statement: Duerosuchus is considered a basal crocodilian closely related to short-snouted forms like alligatoroids.
facts.quote: Duerosuchus es un crocodiliano basal que es considerado como muy cercano a los brevirrostrinos, o crocodilianos de hocico corto, tales como los aligatoroideos.

facts.statement: Duerosuchus lived during the Lutetian stage, between 48.07 and 41.03 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Lutetian (48.07 to 41.03 million years ago)
